title: Designing Visuals with Canva and Free Image Generators

thumbnail.headline: Branded Visuals, Built Fast
thumbnail.image: Navy background, three matching social post cards in indigo and teal with folded fabric, a small spreadsheet row underneath, headline in teal Inter Bold.

slide.title: Branded Visuals, Built Fast
slide.body: Three matching post cards (product image, quote card, tip card) in the same colours and fonts, with a small asset-log row beneath them. Small tag: AI for Content Creators · Lesson 8.

production_notes: Screen demo tools: Canva (free plan) for the brand kit, template and layout, and Google Gemini (image generation in the Gemini app) as the free image generator, per DECISIONS.md. Content.md step 4 uses Canva's own AI image feature; the demo generates the image in Gemini and uploads it to Canva instead. Canva's AI image feature may be shown briefly as an alternative if it is on the free plan.

[VERSION] Canva AI feature names, brand kit availability on the free plan, menu names and plan limits must be checked against the live tool before recording. If the brand kit is not on the free plan, show the colour codes and fonts being set by hand instead.

[VERSION] Gemini image generation limits and licence terms, and whether its images may be used commercially, must be checked before recording. Show the terms check being written in the asset log as a real step.
Gemini adds a visible or invisible mark to generated images on some plans [VERIFY]; do not crop out any visible watermark in the demo.

Fatou and the textile shop in Dakar are fictional. Use a demo Canva account with no personal data visible. No real people, logos, copyrighted characters or named artists' styles in any prompt or image.
The customer review on the quote card must be an invented sample review, shown with the label 'sample'.

Hook.voiceover: People often decide in one second whether to stop at your post, and the visual is usually what they see first. Today, you will watch three branded visuals being built on screen, one with an AI image, and a record of where every image came from.

Explain.voiceover: Last time, we wrote long-form content. Now we design the pictures that go with it. We use two kinds of tool. Canva gives you templates and a brand kit, where you save your colours, fonts and logo. It also has AI features that can suggest designs or remove backgrounds. A free image generator, such as Google Gemini, creates original images from a written prompt.

slide.title: Two kinds of tool
slide.body: Left: Canva: templates · brand kit (colours, fonts, logo) · AI features. Right: Free image generator (demo: Google Gemini): original images from a prompt. Footer: features and licence terms change, check the current version.

Explain.voiceover: A good image prompt has four parts. The subject, what is in the image. The style, such as a realistic photo in soft natural light. The colours, your brand colours in words. And the composition, such as a top view, with empty space on the left for text.

slide.title: Four parts of an image prompt
slide.body: Four puzzle pieces joining into one prompt: Subject ('a bar of yellow soap on a wooden table') · Style ('soft natural light, realistic photo') · Colours ('deep blue, bright teal accents') · Composition ('top view, space on the left for text').

Explain.voiceover: Some safety rules. Do not generate real people, real logos or copyrighted characters. Do not ask for the style of a named living artist. And record the tool and prompt for every AI image, so you can check licences and labels later.
Explain.on_screen_text: No real people, logos or artists' styles

Explain.voiceover: Why does a brand kit matter? It is like a school uniform. Each student is different, but the uniform shows at once which school they belong to. Consistent colours and fonts do the same for your visuals.
Explain.stock_query: students in matching school uniforms walking
Explain.on_screen_text: A brand kit is a uniform

Demonstrate.voiceover: Let's build it. Fatou designs visuals for a sample textile shop in Dakar, Senegal, that sells hand-dyed fabric. She opens Canva and goes to the brand kit. She adds two brand colours by their codes, one font for headings and one for body text.
screen_steps: Open Canva in the browser with a demo account
Go to the brand kit area
Add two brand colours by typing their colour codes: deep indigo and teal
Choose one heading font and one body font
Save the brand kit

Demonstrate.voiceover: She searches templates for Instagram post, and picks a simple layout with space for an image and a short headline. Then she applies her brand kit, and the template changes to her colours and fonts.
screen_steps: Search templates for 'Instagram post'
Choose a simple layout with an image area and a short headline
Apply the brand kit
Show the template colours and fonts switching to indigo, teal and the brand fonts

Demonstrate.voiceover: Now the image. In Google Gemini, she types her prompt: folded hand-dyed cotton fabric in deep indigo and teal patterns, on a light wooden shelf, soft morning light, realistic photo, with empty space at the top.
screen_steps: Open Google Gemini in a new browser tab
Type the prompt: 'Folded hand-dyed cotton fabric in deep indigo and teal patterns, on a light wooden shelf, soft morning light, realistic photo, empty space at the top.'
Send the prompt and wait for the images

Demonstrate.voiceover: She looks closely at the results. She rejects one where the patterns melt into each other, and one with an extra object. She chooses the best image, downloads it, and places it in her Canva template.
screen_steps: Zoom in on each generated image
Point out melting patterns in one image and an extra object in another, and reject both
Download the best image
Upload it to Canva and drag it into the template image area

Demonstrate.voiceover: She adds the headline, new indigo collection, in the brand heading font. Then she zooms out, to check that the text is easy to read on a phone screen. She downloads the design.
screen_steps: Add the headline 'New indigo collection' in the brand heading font
Zoom out to phone size and check the headline is readable
Download the design as an image

Demonstrate.voiceover: Last, she opens her asset log, a simple spreadsheet. She writes the visual's name, the tool, the exact prompt, the date, the plan, and whether she has checked the licence.
screen_steps: Open a spreadsheet named 'Asset log'
Fill one row: visual name · tool (Google Gemini + Canva) · exact prompt · date · plan (free) · licence checked: yes/no

Demonstrate.voiceover: She makes two more visuals in the same style: a quote card with a customer review, and a tip card on washing dyed fabric. The AI image for the tip card shows a label with letters that are not real words. So she removes the label, and adds real text in Canva.
screen_steps: Show the finished quote card with a sample customer review in the same template style
Show the tip card AI image and zoom in on a label with unreadable letters
Cover or crop out the label area
Add real text 'How to wash dyed fabric' with the Canva text tool
Show all three visuals side by side

Demonstrate.voiceover: The common mistake is to accept the first image without looking closely. If an image shows your product, it must look like your real product, or customers may feel misled. Zoom in and check every detail.

Recap.voiceover: Let's recap. First, Canva's brand kit and templates keep your colours, fonts and layout consistent. Second, a good image prompt describes subject, style, colours and composition. Third, avoid real people, logos, copyrighted characters and named artists' styles, and log the tool, prompt and licence check for every AI image.

slide.title: Key takeaways
slide.body: 1. Brand kit + templates = consistent visuals. 2. Prompt: subject, style, colours, composition. 3. Stay safe and log every AI image.

CTA.voiceover: Now it is your turn. In the exercise below, create three branded visuals in Canva, with at least one AI-generated image. Record the tool and prompt for each image, and check the licence terms. It takes about thirty-five minutes. In the next lesson, Short Video with CapCut, we add movement. See you there.
